Let's denote the indefinite integral by $I=\int \frac{{ln}^{6}⁡x}{x}\,\text{d}x.$

To use integration by parts, let's suppose that

$$
\begin{aligned}u={ln}^{6}⁡x & \,⇒\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{6{ln}^{5}⁡x}{x}\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x} & \,⇒\,v=\int \frac{1}{x}\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =\int \frac{{ln}^{6}⁡x}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =({ln}^{6}⁡x)(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)-\int (\operatorname{ln}⁡x)(\frac{6{ln}^{5}⁡x}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={ln}^{7}⁡x-6\int \frac{{ln}^{6}⁡x}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={ln}^{7}⁡x-6I.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for $I.$ We can ignore the constant of integration in this case, because it is insignificant for further evaluation of the definite integral.

$$
\begin{aligned}I & ={ln}^{7}⁡x-6I \\ 7I & ={ln}^{7}⁡x \\ I & =\frac{{ln}^{7}⁡x}{7}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate our definite integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{{ln}^{6}⁡x}{x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{7}({ln}^{7}⁡x){|}_{1}^{e} \\  & =\frac{1}{7}({ln}^{7}⁡(e)-{ln}^{7}⁡(1)) \\  & =\frac{1}{7}\end{aligned}
$$
